none: Verse text only; no commentary point is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ, with light or doubled thāʾ, is grass, plants, and scraps cast by a flood onto a valley's edge; an unnamed poet uses it for torrent debris.
rows.anchor: ما يقذف به السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports al-ighthāʾ as a plural; Abū Ḥayyān calls it unusual because it forms afʿāl from fiʿāl.
rows.anchor: ورواه الفرّاء : والإغثاء على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥuwwa is a black tint tending toward green; Dhū al-Rummah's poem uses it for a woman's lips and gums.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرّمة : لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second gloss is green with black; another poetic usage describes aḥwāʾ as a gazelle with two black and white stripes on its back.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خضرة عليها سواد ،   والأحوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gazelle sense is specified as having two black and white stripes along its back, with a poem cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: والأحوى : الظبي الذي في ظهره خطان من سواد وبياض

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ glosses al-ḥuwwa as brownness.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح : الحوة : سمرة ،   وقال الأعلم

rows.speaker: الأعلم
rows.claim: Al-Aʿlam first describes the color as tending toward black.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعلم : لون يضرب إلى السواد

rows.speaker: الأعلم
rows.claim: Al-Aʿlam also describes it as intense green tending toward black.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضاً : الشديد الخضرة التي تضرب إلى السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes aḥwāʾ an adjective qualifying ghuthāʾ.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أحوى صفة لغثاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says old flood debris turns black and rots when rain reaches it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى { فجعله غثاء أحوى } : أي أسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, aḥwāʾ is a circumstantial accusative of al-marʿā, intensely green and tending to black through plentiful water.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أحوى حال من المرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective is delayed to suit the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وحسن تأخير أحوى لأجل الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further poem describes rain and its luxuriant growth.
rows.anchor: وقال : وغيث من الوسمي حوتلاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading takes the exception as intentional and substantive.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه استثناء مقصود

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: They take the exception as material God decreed to abrogate, removing its recitation and ruling.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما : مما قضى الله نسخه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God may make the Prophet forget something so he can establish it as Sunnah; the Prophet says he forgets and is made to forget for that purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view allows a lapse that God later brings back to the Prophet's memory; a Prophetic report recalls verses brought to mind by ʿAbbād ibn Bishr's recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن يغلبك النسيان عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes فلا تنسى as not abandoning practice, except where God wills to abrogate the ruling.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { فلا تنسى } : أي فلا تترك العمل به

rows.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
rows.claim: They call the exception a conventional filler with no actual matter excepted, following an Arab usage.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة : هذا استثناء صلة في الكلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adopts this view to deny forgetting altogether, using a small exception formula as negation, like calling someone one's partner in all property except what God wills.
rows.anchor: وأخذ الزمخشري هذا القول فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Farrāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī because their account makes the exception no exception, unsuitable even in eloquent speech.
rows.anchor: وقول الفراء والزمخشري يجعل الاستثناء كلا استثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects the weak claim that lā is prohibitive and the alif remains only to maintain the rhyme.
rows.anchor: وكذلك القول بأن لا في { فلا تنسى } للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to teach the Prophet the recitation; he will forget only by God's will through abrogation, a lapse establishing Sunnah, or a lapse followed by reminder.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه تعالى أخبر أنه سيقرئه ،   وأنه لا ينسى إلا ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is protected from forgetting what he is commanded to convey; any lapse occurs only in one of the stated ways.
rows.anchor: وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم من النسيان فيما أمر بتبليغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of recitation follows the command to glorify God: glorification entails reciting revealed Qurʾān, and the Prophet feared forgetting it, so God reassures him.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة { سنقرئك } لما قبله : أنه لما أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the Prophet's aloud recitation and his inward fear that the revelation might slip away; His knowledge encompasses all things.
rows.anchor: { إنه يعلم الجهر } : أي جهرك بالقرآن ،   { وما يخفى } : أي في نفسك من خوف التفلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is coordinated with sanuqriʾuka; the intervening emphatic clause is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: { ونيسرك } معطوف على { سنقرئك } ،   وما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides the Prophet along the easiest way, specifically making revelation easy for him to memorize.
rows.anchor: أي يوفقك للطريقة التي هي أيسر وأسهل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes al-yusrā as the easy, monotheistic religious law.
rows.anchor: في حفظ الوحي . وقيل : للشريعة الحنيفية السهلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God leads him to good worldly and otherworldly outcomes: victory, rank, and elevation in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يذهب بك إلى الأمور الحسنة في أمر دنياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After promising recitation and ease, God commands reminding: recitation should benefit the Prophet himself and those to whom he was sent.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر أنه يقرئه وييسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conditional makes the command depend on benefit, but it rebukes Quraysh by implying these obstinate people are unlikely to benefit.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأمر بالتذكير مشروط بنفع الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition functions as a rebuke, like telling someone to call another person if he hears; the cited poem says there is no life in the listener.
rows.anchor: فهو كما قال الشاعر : لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حياً

rows.speaker: الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني
rows.claim: They understand the sense as reminding even if it does not benefit, with one stated case implying the other.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء والنحاس والزهراوي والجرجاني معناه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes in as meaning idh, as in the statement that believers are superior when they believe.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن بمعنى إذ ،   كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the fearful take heed: fear moves them to consider how to escape what they dread, and reflection leads to truth; these are scholars and believers according to their guidance.
rows.anchor: فإن الخوف حامل على النظر في الذي ينجيه مما يخافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the reminder, which the most wretched person avoids.
rows.anchor: { الأشقى } : أي المبالغ في الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's unbeliever is the most wretched among disbelievers, while one who believes in him and his message surpasses believers in earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: لأن الكافر بالرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم هو أشقى الكفار

words: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned person neither dies to rest nor lives a pleasant life.
rows.anchor: { ثم لا يموت } : فيستريح ،   { ولا يحيى } حياة هنيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma signals gradation in severity: suspension between life and death is more dreadful than burning in the fire.
rows.anchor: وجيء بثم المقتضية للتراخي إيذاناً بتفاوت مراتب الشدة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb in the second person, addressing the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { بل تؤثرون } بتاء الخطاب للكفار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view addresses both righteous and wicked: the righteous prefer worldly life to gain reward, while the wicked prefer it from desire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خطاب للبر والفاجر ؛ يؤثرها البر

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والزعفراني وابن مقسم
rows.claim: These readers, including ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan, and Abū ʿAmr, read the verb in the third person with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري

none: Verse text only; no commentary point is given.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarīr take this to refer to the statement that the purified succeed and people prefer worldly life; Abū Ḥayyān favors this because the referent is nearby.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد وابن جرير ،   ويرجح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, and al-Suddī take this to refer to the sūra's teachings.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعكرمة والسدي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the referent is the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : إلى القرآن . وقال قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah identifies the referent as the statement that the afterlife is better and more lasting.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : إلى قوله : { والآخرة خير وأبقى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The success of the purified and the superiority and permanence of the afterlife were never abrogated: they appeared in earlier scriptures and remain in the final law.
rows.anchor: لم ينسخ إفلاح من تزكى ،   والآخرة خير وأبقى في شرع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority pronounce the ḥāʾ in al-ṣuḥuf with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : الصحف بضم الحاء

rows.speaker: الأعمش وهرون وعصمة عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hārūn, and ʿIṣmah, both transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read the word with a quiescent ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: والأعمش وهرون وعصمة ،   كلاهما عن أبي عمرو : بسكونها

rows.speaker: كتاب اللوامح العبقلي عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Lawāmiʿ al-ʿAqbali reports Abū ʿAmr reading both forms with a quiescent ḥāʾ, a Tamīm dialect.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب اللوامح العبقلي عن أبي عمرو : الصحف صحف بإسكان الحاء فيهما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read Ibrāhīm with alif, yāʾ, and kasra on hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : إبراهيم بألف وبياء والهاء مكسورة

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء
rows.claim: Abū Rajāʾ omits the alif and yāʾ; the source describes the hāʾ vowels as both fatḥa and kasra.
rows.anchor: وأبو رجاء : بحذفهما والهاء مفتوحة مكسورة معاً

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Ibn al-Zubayr read Abrahām with alif throughout the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وأبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير : أبراهام بألف في كل القرآن

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār reads Ibrāhīm with alif, fatḥa on hāʾ, and no yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ومالك بن دينار : إبراهيم بألف وفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah reads it with kasra on hāʾ and no yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وعبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة : إبراهيم بكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khālawayh also records Ibrāhīm with alif and ḍamma on hāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خالويه : وقد جاء إبراهيم ،   يعني بألف وضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that the scrolls of Abraham and Moses were discussed earlier in his commentary on Sūrat al-Najm.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في والنجم الكلام على صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging reflection, God commands the Messenger to remind them and not be troubled if they do not reflect.
rows.anchor: ولما حضهم على النظر ،   أمر رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتذكيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's role is only to remind, as in the statement that he is responsible only for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: { إنما أنت مذكر } ،   كقوله تعالى : { إن عليك إلا البلاغ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhaymin means one who exercises authority, as in the statement that the Messenger is not a tyrant over them.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { وما أنت عليهم بجبار }

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن عامر وحمزة وهارون
rows.claim: The majority read with ṣād and kasra on ṭāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir, Qunbul's transmitter Nuṭayq, and Ḥafṣ's transmitter Zarʿān have sīn; Ḥamzah has an imāla toward zāy; Hārūn opens ṭāʾ, a Tamīm dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : بالصاد وكسر الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayṭara is transitive, as shown by its inchoative form tasattara; this pattern includes only musayṭir, muhaymin, mubayṭir, and mubayqir.
rows.anchor: وسيطر متعد عندهم ويدل عليه فعل المطاوعة وهو تسطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley names Mujaymir and Mudyabir may be diminutives of Mujmar and Mudbar.
rows.anchor: وجاء مجيمر اسم واد ومديبر ،   ويمكن أن يكون أصلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Hell is compared with the verse saying that Hell will be exposed for anyone to see.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmaʾidhin is an apposition to idhā. Al-Zamakhsharī says yatadhakkaru governs both; Abū Ḥayyān notes the common view instead repeats the governor in ellipsis.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلامه أن العامل في البدل هو العامل نفسه في المبدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person then remembers what he neglected in the world.
rows.anchor: أي يتذكر ما فرط فيه . { وأنى له الذكرى }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The reminder's benefit is unavailable then; had the person taken heed in worldly life, it would have benefited him in the next life.
rows.anchor: لو اتعظ في الدنيا لنفعه ذلك في الأخرى ،   قاله الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najd means a neck, with plural nujūd.
rows.anchor: النجد : العنق وجمعه نجود ،   وبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najd means a high road; the region takes its name from elevation above low-lying Tihāmah.
rows.anchor: وبه سميت نجد لارتفاعها عن انخفاض تهامة ،   والنجد : الطريق العالي

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's verse is cited as poetic evidence for the term's usage.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس : فريقان منهم جازع بطن نخله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and most commentators understand the two roads as the paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وابن عباس والجمهور : طريق الخير والشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي وابن المسيب والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also, with ʿAlī, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, interprets them as the two breasts, routes for the child's life and nourishment.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضاً ،   وعليّ وابن المسيب والضحاك : الثديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs is a generic singular, as the following reference to its inspiration confirms; the fa in the next verse orders inspiration after the adjustment that entails intellect.
rows.anchor: اسم جنس ،   ويدل على ذلك ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's fashioning of the soul completes its intellect and capacity for reflection, explaining why inspiration follows.
rows.anchor: وتسويتها : إكمال عقلها ونظرها ،   ولذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers the possibility that the indefinite noun means Adam's particular soul; Abū Ḥayyān finds this unlikely because the following descriptions suit a generic soul.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : لم نكرت النفس ؟ قلت : فيه وجهان

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses alhamahā as making it adhere to its disposition.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جبير : ألزمها . وقال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses alhamahā as making it know.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : عرفها . وقال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses alhamahā as making it clear to the soul.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : بين لها . وقال الزجاج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God guides the soul to piety and abandons it with respect to wickedness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : وفقها للتقوى ،   وألهمها فجورها : أي خذلها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God informs the soul and gives it power to acquire either wickedness or piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عرفها وجعل لها قوة يصح معها اكتساب الفجور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says inspiration means understanding which path is good or bad and being empowered to choose; he cites the next verses as making the person agent of purification. Abū Ḥayyān calls this a hint of Muʿtazilism.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامها وإعقالها

rows.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others say this is the oath's answer; the lām is omitted because the statement is long, with laqad aflaha understood.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره : هذا جواب القسم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the oath's answer is omitted and estimates it as la-tubʿathunna, you will surely be resurrected.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجواب محذوف تقديره لتبعثن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī estimates the answer as God's destruction of Mecca's people for rejecting His Messenger, as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ; he treats this verse as an aside.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means the soul's emergence and growth through righteous deeds; concealment hides and degrades it through sins.
rows.anchor: وزكاؤها : ظهورها ونماؤها بالعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: The apparent agent of both verbs is the pronoun referring back to man.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن فاعل زكى ودسى ضمير يعود على من ،   وقاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās allows the pronoun to refer to God, with feminine agreement because man is understood as soul.
rows.anchor: وقائل ذلك هو بحر العلم عبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet would pray on reciting the verse: O God, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it and its guardian and master.
rows.anchor: كان عليه السلام إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال : « اللهم آت نفسي تقواها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attacks the divine-agent reading as Qadarite blame of God.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : وأما قول من زعم أن الضمير في زكى ودسى لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī follows his habit of insulting Sunnis; Ibn ʿAbbās held the view, and the Prophet's supplication supports it.
rows.anchor: فجرى على عادته في سب أهل السنة . هذا ،   وقائل ذلك هو بحر العلم عبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadsiyah means concealment, from d-s-s; the third doubled consonant is replaced by a weak letter, as in the cited form naqaṣ.
rows.anchor: التدسية : الإخفاء ،   وأصله دسس فأبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line using dassasta, and another line about burying ʿAmr, support the sense of concealment.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : وأنت الذي دسست عمراً فأصبحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may conceal oneself among righteous people through hypocrisy without belonging to them.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى : { دساها } في أهل الخير بالرياء وليس منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning piety is followed by the success of the one who purifies the soul; mentioning concealment is followed by the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولما قال : { وقد خاب من دساها } ،   أعقبه بأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير والبزي والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs; al-Bazzī doubles tāʾ, while the majority read one tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير : تتلظى بتاءين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ibtighāʾ in the accusative as a disconnected exception, since it is not included among the favors.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { إلا ابتغاء } بنصب الهمزة ،   وهو استثناء منقطع

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads in the nominative as an apposition to niʿmah, also nominative, following Tamīm usage; poetry is cited for both case forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب : بالرفع على البدل في موضع نعمة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads the word in a shortened form without hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : { إلا ابتغاء } ،   مقصوراً

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows ibtighāʾ to be an object of purpose by sense: he gives wealth to seek his Lord's face, not to repay favors.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : ويجوز أن يكون ابتغاء وجه الله مفعولاً له

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives the same semantic analysis: wealth is not given for recompense but to seek God's face.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : ونصب على تأويل ما أعطيك ابتغاء جزائك

rows.speaker: الجمهور وعروة بن الزبير وهشام وأبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: The majority read waddʿaka with doubled dāl; ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, his son Hishām, Abū Ḥaywah, Abū Baḥriyyah, and Ibn Abī ʿAblah lighten it, meaning abandoned you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ما ودعك } بتشديد الدال ؛ وعروة بن الزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In eloquent Arabic, taraka replaces wadaʿa and wadhara in verb, participle, and verbal noun forms, though both verbs are attested.
rows.anchor: واستغنت العرب في فصيح كلامها بترك عن ودع ووذر

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود
rows.claim: Abū al-Aswad's poem uses wadaʿa, illustrating that the verb is attested.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الأسود : ليت شعري عن خليلي ما الذي

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: A second, unnamed poet also uses the verb wadaʿa.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : وثم ودعنا آل عمرو وعامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawdiʿ intensifies abandonment: someone who bids farewell while leaving has greatly abandoned the person.
rows.anchor: والتوديع مبالغة في الودع ،   لأن من ودعك مفارقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalā means to hate; the usual present is yaqlā, while Ṭayyiʾ has taʿlā with fatḥa on ʿayn.
rows.anchor: { وما قلى } : ما أبغضك ،   واللغة الشهيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun referring to the Messenger is elided for brevity in qalā and the following verbs awā, hadā, and aghnā.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول اختصاراً في { قلى } ،   وفي { فآوى }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say revelation paused once in Mecca, distressing the Prophet; Umm Jamīl taunted that his satan had left him, and the sūra was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره : أبطأ الوحي مرة على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بمكة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Gabriel's visit was delayed because a puppy was in the Prophet's house.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : إنما احتبس عنه جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others say the two terms refer to the two abodes, this world and the next.
rows.anchor: يريد الدارين ،   قاله ابن إسحاق وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah suggests they may be the Prophet's states before and after the sūra, with a promise of victory and triumph.
rows.anchor: وعده تعالى بالنصر والظفر ،   قاله ابن عطية اهتمالاً

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links this to the preceding denial of abandonment: continued revelation and God's love are supreme honor, so the Prophet's afterlife will be greater, with precedence over prophets, his community's witness, and intercession raising believers' ranks.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : كيف اتصل قوله

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the promised giving and satisfaction to concern the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور : ذلك في الآخرة . وقال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet's satisfaction means none of his household will enter Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : رضاه أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says the Prophet was promised a thousand palaces in Paradise with needed blessings and servants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : رضاه أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار . وقال أيضاً : رضاه أنه وعده بألف قصر في الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places the promise in this life, including the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الدنيا بفتح مكة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers an inclusive promise: worldly victory and the reward stored for the Prophet in the next life.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن هذا موعد شامل لما أعطاه في الدنيا من الظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in both this verse and the previous one is an emphatic lām of inception; here an implicit subject means 'and surely you will be given.'
rows.anchor: { وللآخرة } لام ابتداء أكدت مضمون الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laying the burden aside is a metaphor for the Prophet's protection from sins and purification from impurities, stressing their complete absence.
rows.anchor: كناية عن عصمته من الذنوب وتطهيره من الأدناس

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lexicographers say a load anqaḍa a camel's back when strain makes it creak; naqīḍ al-mirjal is the pot's creak.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة : أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة

rows.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
rows.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse says the burden of caring for his people made his back creak.
rows.anchor: قال عباس بن مرداس : وأنقض ظهري ما تطويت منهم

rows.speaker: جميل
rows.claim: Jamīl's verse uses naqīḍ for the sound of ropes coming apart.
rows.anchor: وقال جميل : وحتى تداعت بالنقيض حباله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqīḍ denotes the sound of something breaking or coming loose.
rows.anchor: والنقيض : صوت الانقضاض والانفكاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet's mention by joining it with His own in the testimony of faith, call to prayer, iqāmah, tashahhud, sermons, Qurʾān, titles, earlier scriptures, and the covenant with prophets and their peoples to believe in him.
rows.anchor: هو أن قرنه بذكره تعالى في كلمة الشهادة والأذان

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Ḥassān's poem says God joined the Prophet's name to His in the muezzin's testimony at each of the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال حسان : أغر عليه للنبوة خاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listing these blessings implies that God will also grant victory over the Prophet's enemies.
rows.anchor: وتعديد هذه النعم عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم يقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated promise intensifies the certainty of ease.
rows.anchor: ثم كرر ذلك مبالغة في حصول اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease follows hardship without a long interval, so it is portrayed as accompanying it and promises the Prophet near relief.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اليسر يعتقب العسر من غير تطاول أزمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the two eases as different in setting: one in this world, one in the next.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تكرر اليسر باعتبار المحل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says each hardship has an ease because hardship is definite while ease is indefinite, so the first ease differs from the second.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مع كل عسر يسر ،   إن من حيث أن العسر

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith states that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : « لن يغلب عسر يسرين »

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو جعفر وعيسى والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb, Abū Jaʿfar, and ʿĪsā pronounce sīn in both al-ʿusr and yusr with ḍamma; the majority use sukūn.
rows.anchor: وضم سين العسر ويسراً فيهن ابن وثاب وأبو جعفر وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing God's favors and promise of ease, the Prophet is told to persist in worship when he finishes one task, without slackening.
rows.anchor: ولما عدد تعالى نعمه السابقة عليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that after an obligatory duty, the Prophet should engage in supererogatory worship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : { فإذا فرغت } من فرضك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also interprets the command as performing night prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : { فإذا فرغت } من فرضك ،   { فانصب } في التنفل عبادة لربك . وقال أيضاً : { فانصب } في قيام الليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says that when worldly work ends, the Prophet should devote himself to worship.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : قال { فإذا فرغت } من شغل دنياك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah say that after prayer the Prophet should devote himself to supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة : { فإذا فرغت } من الصلاة ،   { فانصب } في الدعاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that after jihad the Prophet should devote himself to worship; Abū Ḥayyān objects that jihad was prescribed in Medina.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : { فإذا فرغت } من الجهاد ،   { فانصب } في العبادة . ويعترض قوله هذا بأن الجهاد فرض بالمدينة

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو السمال
rows.claim: The majority read faraghta with fatḥa on rāʾ; Abū al-Sammāl uses kasra as a dialect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فرغت } بفتح الراء ؛ وأبو السمال : بكسرها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the kasra form non-eloquent.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ليست بفصيحة

rows.speaker: الجمهور وقوم
rows.claim: The majority read fanṣab with a quiescent bāʾ and no gemination; another group doubles it with fatḥa, from anṣāb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فانصب } بسكون الباء خفيفة ،   وقوم : بشدها مفتوحة

rows.speaker: آخرون من الإمامية
rows.claim: Some Imāmī readers read fanṣib with kasra on ṣād, meaning appoint a successor after finishing the message.
rows.anchor: وقرأ آخرون من الإمامية : فانصب بكسر الصاد بمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah calls the Imāmī reading anomalous and weak in meaning, and says it is not established from a scholar.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وهي قراءة شاذة ضعيفة المعنى لم تثبت عن عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading is an imperative from the basic triliteral verb: direct all desires to God alone, never to another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فارغب } ،   أمر من رغب ثلاثياً

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAblah read the form with a doubled ghayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وابن أبي عبلة : فرغت ،   أمر من رغب
